repeatable.cadence: once per household per equipment upgrade

who_pays: No single payer — remaining heat-pump rebates come from state and utility programs; the federal 25C $2,000 credit expired Dec 31, 2025.

what_gets_accepted: Varies by program; participating contractor and listed equipment usually required.

who_pays: State/utility insulation rebate programs; the federal 25C insulation credit (up to $1,200/year) expired Dec 31, 2025.
who_qualifies: Anyone can look up; qualifying requires a live utility insulation rebate and often pre-approval or an energy audit before the work.
work_available: Not work — a directory of rebates; remaining utility rebates are typically a few hundred dollars, not $1,000.
what_gets_accepted: Varies by program; many require pre-approval or an energy audit BEFORE the work — doing the work first can disqualify you.
costs_and_unpaid_time: You must pay for the insulation work first — this is a discount on spending, not money earned.
when_cash_arrives: Utility rebates typically paid 4–8 weeks after the insulation work is completed and documented.

costs_and_unpaid_time: No fee to claim; the heat-pump purchase and installation is the cost.
demand_side: Energy Trust of Oregon funds the incentives; demand is the program's energy-efficiency goals among its member utilities' Oregon customers.

who_pays: T-Mobile, which reimburses your old carrier's device balance to win you as a customer.

work_available: One-time per new account — not work; only pays if you actually owe a device balance or early termination fee.

costs_and_unpaid_time: No fee to claim; you must owe the balance being reimbursed — no balance, no payout.
when_cash_arrives: Card typically arrives within 15 days after the reimbursement submission is approved.
demand_side: T-Mobile itself funds the reimbursement to acquire new subscribers from rival carriers.

who_pays: The federal LIHEAP program, administered by each state — funds go to your energy vendor, never to you.
who_qualifies: Household income at or below 150% of the poverty line (or 60% of state median income); funding is limited and applications are only open in each state's seasonal window.
work_available: Not work — bill assistance for income-eligible households; only a fraction of eligible households are served each year.
what_gets_accepted: Income-eligible households applying within their state's seasonal window; you never receive cash — the benefit (about $380 average heating) is paid directly to your energy vendor.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No cost; unpaid time is the application and waiting.
when_cash_arrives: Once approved, the benefit is paid directly to the household's energy vendor, typically within weeks; crisis assistance for shutoff emergencies is expedited.

repeatable.cadence: annual — one benefit per heating season while income-eligible

demand_side: The federal government funds LIHEAP; state agencies distribute it to income-eligible households.

who_pays: The federal Weatherization Assistance Program, delivered by state agencies — you get free home improvements, $0 in cash.
who_qualifies: Household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty line; renters need written landlord permission.
work_available: Not work — free weatherization for income-eligible homes; about 32,000 homes/year nationally, so waitlists of months are normal.
what_gets_accepted: Approved applicants get free weatherization work scheduled by the state agency; it lowers bills (about $372/year average savings) but never pays cash.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No cost; unpaid time is the application and the months-long wait.
when_cash_arrives: No fixed payout — free services are scheduled after application approval; savings accrue as lower energy bills.

repeatable.cadence: once per home per program cycle

demand_side: The DOE funds WAP; state agencies deliver it to income-eligible households.
